small_guidance:
- Add larger tile configs to the autotune sweep for the 1024×8192×8192 GEMM (e.g. BLOCK_M=128/BLOCK_N=256/BLOCK_K=64 num_warps=8 num_stages=3-4, BLOCK_M=256/BLOCK_N=128/BLOCK_K=64) — K=8192 is large so deeper pipelining (num_stages=4) should overlap loads better.
- Pre-transpose weight once in `__init__` (store W as (K, N) contiguous) so the inner B load is contiguous along N (`stride_bk=N, stride_bn=1`) instead of the current `stride_bk=1, stride_bn=K` strided pattern, which hurts vectorized loads on the hot K loop.
- Drop the per-iter K mask: since K=8192 is divisible by BLOCK_K, hoist the mask out of the loop (unmasked loads inside, single tail iter outside) to cut address math in the inner loop.
large_guidance:
- Fuse the softmax into the matmul epilogue using a split-K-free, N-complete tile: since N=8192 fits a row, make the kernel persistent per row-tile (BLOCK_M rows × full N) — accumulate the full row of GELU outputs in SRAM/registers across BLOCK_N column passes, compute row max + sum online, then write normalized softmax. Eliminates the entire second kernel's read+write of the M×N tensor (~256MB traffic).
- Alternatively, two-pass fused design: pass 1 computes matmul+GELU and per-row max/sum simultaneously (one program per row-block streams across N), pass 2 recomputes or reads tile and normalizes. Use online softmax (Welford-style running max/sum) so only one matmul pass is needed and the GELU output need not be re-materialized fully.
- Consider running the GEMM in TF32 (`tl.dot(..., allow_tf32=True)`) or fp16 accumulate-to-fp32 to roughly 2× the matmul throughput on the 4090; the linear+GELU+softmax tolerance (5e-2) easily accommodates TF32.
